A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures and appendices. The retained material, appendix relocation and additions can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–4 report original simulations of ridge regression, random ReLU-feature models and trained two-layer ReLU networks, including hyperparameter sweeps.

after.justification: V3 retains these original simulations and adds experiments on threshold accuracy, Gaussian label noise and random Fourier features in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The ridge objective, fixed-feature linear model, GD updates and existing ReLU training procedures are unchanged. The Fourier-feature experiment instantiates the already general fixed-feature framework.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds synthetic regression with Gaussian-corrupted labels and learning a single Fourier-feature teacher. The existing realizable linear, non-realizable ReLU-feature and zero-teacher neural-network tasks remain.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing baseline algorithms against a proposed method. Comparisons remain between training and test behavior, theoretical bounds and empirical observations, or hyperparameter choices.

E3.justification: Existing Section 5 settings remain unchanged. Appendix B introduces threshold accuracy using squared error at most 0.01, noise controls with standard deviations 0.01, 0.05 and 0.1, and configurations for the added experiments.

E4.justification: Figure 5 adds a paired comparison of squared loss and threshold accuracy from the same simulation. Figure 6 adds label-noise robustness and sensitivity analysis. The original hyperparameter sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: The new Figure 5 explicitly discloses that its two plots come from one simulation. Figure 1's reporting of 50 independent runs is unchanged; no increase in existing run counts or new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Figures 1–4 retain identical results. New Figures 5–7 report an accuracy plateau, grokking under Gaussian label noise with little timing variation across the tested noise levels, and delayed generalization with Fourier features. These are additional findings under supplementary conditions.

T1.justification: The main theorem statements and Appendix A proofs are unchanged apart from a cross-reference. V3 removes v1's Lemma B.7 on Gaussian sample-covariance eigenvalue deviations and adds the threshold-accuracy definition. Lemmas B.1–B.6 are retained as C.1–C.6.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the three-stage grokking guarantee, quantitative hyperparameter dependence, nonlinear-network empirical extension and first-end-to-end-result novelty claim. Added emphasis on linearity restates the existing contribution's scope.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations involving changes in implicit priors and metric-dependent accuracy plateaus. It also suggests applicability to decaying step sizes and gradient flow, explicitly discusses noisy-label theory as open, and notes careful tuning for Fourier features. Existing core mechanism explanations and proof limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies hyperparameters for the new experiments, Gaussian label-noise generation details, and the Fourier-feature construction with Gaussian frequencies and uniform phases. Existing implementation descriptions remain; no new code or data access information is provided.

R1.justification: V3 adds Gunasekar et al. (2018), Vardi and Shamir (2021), and Lauditi et al. (2025) for the implicit-bias discussion, and removes Wainwright (2019) with Lemma B.7. Section 1.1 also adds context about grokking without explicit regularization; core novelty positioning remains.

P1.justification: Localized prose edits and expanded discussion accompany new acknowledgements and an experiments appendix, with former Appendix B becoming C. Affiliations and the publication footer are updated. Main section order and most exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds three appendix figures showing paired accuracy/loss curves, noise comparisons and Fourier-feature training. Original Figures 1–4 retain their graphics and captions. Text reflows, but the overall layout and existing displays are preserved.

improvement.justification: Appendix B's metric comparison and noise tests improve the empirical characterization, while the Fourier example adds supporting coverage and the central proofs remain intact. The gains are limited: Figure 5 uses one simulation, and Section 6's new minimum-norm interpolation interpretation lacks an explicit zero-regularization qualification. These qualifications temper the useful supplementary evidence.
